our_view.thesis_status: Post-restructuring operating trends are improving off the trough: June 2026 marks three straight months of rising revenue and Reported EBITDA, weak sites down to 8 (from a peak of 9), and agency-labor dependence down to 10.0% of revenue (from a Q4 2025 peak of 17.6%) -- consistent with pillars 1 and 4 holding and pillar 2 showing real, if partial, progress (graded 'pressured' rather than 'intact' since 8 of 15 sites remain unprofitable and revenue is still ~17% below the approved budget and well below the pre-2025 run-rate). Pillar 3 (covenant reinstatement) is graded 'pressured': the informational FCCR has WORSENED every quarter since the restructuring closed (1.05x at 2025-Q4 -> 0.67x at 2026-Q1 -> 0.37x at 2026-Q2), purely on trailing-twelve-month math still absorbing the 2025 collapse -- it should mechanically improve through year-end as those months roll off, but that has not yet been demonstrated. The September 30, 2026 FCCR reinstatement-readiness milestone (Stabilization Milestone M4, PENDING) is the key near-term test, due in two weeks from this review. Restructuring accounting (TDR framework, instrument-level test, goodwill interim reassessment) remains PROVISIONAL nearly six months after close, which is itself worth escalating if it persists much longer.
our_view.what_would_change_our_mind: A fourth consecutive month of EBITDA/revenue improvement with weak-site count at or below 8 and agency-labor % holding near or below 10% would support upgrading trajectory further and reconsidering watchlist status. Conversely, a reversal of June's improvement, a missed or unfavorable September 30 FCCR reinstatement-readiness milestone, or the provisional restructuring/goodwill accounting resolving unfavorably (a larger loss, higher carrying debt, or an additional impairment) would move this back toward 'deteriorating' and keep or deepen the watchlist flag.

entries.line: Operating lease / facility rent expense (embedded within 'Occupancy and site costs' and other cost lines; not a separately labeled Income Statement row)
entries.limb: Structural component of the credit agreement's Covenant EBITDA / Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio construction -- operating lease expense is excluded from the EBITDA numerator and the SAME rent payment is instead counted as a 'Lease payments' component of Fixed Charges in the denominator (reverse-engineered from the 2026-Q2 Covenant Calculation TTM Detail; the actual agreement limb text was not directly quotable from the fictional clean-room summary and should be confirmed by covenant-setup against the A&R Agreement's own EBITDA and Fixed Charges definitions).
entries.reason: This is a MECHANICAL, PERMANENT feature of how the agreement defines Covenant EBITDA and Fixed Charges -- not a discretionary or one-time election. It is CONSTANT every month: exactly $553,353.26/month ($6,640,239.12/year), matching the '2025 facility lease expense included above' figure from the Goodwill Impairment Support workpaper. Verified against 12 consecutive months (2025-07 through 2026-06): Covenant EBITDA (per Covenant Calculation TTM Detail) minus Reported EBITDA (per each month's Income Statement) equals exactly $553,353.26 every single month with no exceptions. TTM Reported EBITDA at June 2026 was actually NEGATIVE (-$226,820.42) even though TTM Covenant EBITDA was +$6,413,418.70 (informational FCCR 0.3682x) -- since the same rent dollar is already captured in the Fixed Charges denominator, this construction is not obviously more lenient than treating rent as a normal opex, but it DOES mean 'Covenant EBITDA' materially overstates the company's true, reported operating cash generation on a standalone basis, which matters for how the credit read should be framed.
